purpose: Generation + engine profile resolver for AUTOHAWK. This prevents mixing Golf 4, Golf 5, Golf 6, Golf 7 etc. into one market/risk bucket.
rules: Generation matters more than broad model name.
Engine and gearbox can completely change flip risk.
Use generation price bands as conservative buy discipline, not absolute market truth.
If generation or engine is unknown, keep as CHECK unless price/TUV/service proof is strong.

generations.name: Golf 4
generations.notes: Old but still liquid only when very cheap. TUV, rust and exact engine decide everything. A normal Golf 4 is not a strong lead above about 1600-1800 EUR unless condition is unusually clean.

engines.label: 1.6 SR/MPI petrol
engines.notes: Best simple Golf 4 petrol profile. Saleable if rust/TUV are good.

engines.label: 1.4 petrol
engines.notes: Weak motor. Only interesting cheap with long TUV and clean body.

engines.label: 1.8T petrol
engines.notes: Enthusiast demand but tuning/turbo/abuse risk. Not beginner stock.

engines.label: 1.9 TDI
engines.notes: Very durable reputation. Age, rust, turbo, clutch/DMF and TUV decide.

engines.label: automatic gearbox risk
engines.notes: Old automatic reduces cheap flip safety; test shifting hot/cold.

generations.name: Golf 5
generations.notes: Very liquid, but many are normal market cars. Best flip profile is 1.6 MPI manual with TUV. Avoid FSI/TSI/DSG unless price is very low and proof exists.

engines.label: 1.6 MPI petrol manual
engines.notes: Best Golf 5 petrol buyer story. Check rust, clutch, cooling, oil leaks.

engines.label: 1.4 petrol
engines.notes: Weak. Good only cheap with TUV; not worth overpaying.

engines.label: 1.6 FSI
engines.notes: NOx/injector/carbon reputation. Keep CHECK unless proof and discount are strong.

engines.label: 1.4 TSI EA111
engines.notes: Chain/oil/turbo market fear. No HOT without chain/turbo proof.

engines.label: 1.9 TDI
engines.notes: Good reputation, but clutch/DMF/turbo/rust and mileage matter.

engines.label: 2.0 TDI
engines.notes: Can sell, but injectors/turbo/DPF/EGR/belt proof required.

engines.label: DSG/DQ200/S-tronic risk
engines.notes: Market fear. Test mechatronic/clutch; no strong lead without proof.

generations.name: Golf 6
generations.notes: Modern enough and liquid, but wrong engine/gearbox can destroy margin. 1.6 MPI/manual is safest, 1.4 TSI/DSG needs strict proof.

engines.label: 1.6 MPI petrol manual
engines.notes: Safer Golf 6 petrol profile. Verify it is not FSI/TSI.

engines.label: 1.2 TSI EA111
engines.notes: Timing chain/tensioner risk. Needs invoice proof.

engines.label: 1.4 TSI EA111
engines.notes: High chain/oil/turbo fear. Only with proof and deep discount.

engines.label: 1.6 TDI
engines.notes: DPF/EGR/injector risk. Good only with service and long TUV.

engines.label: 2.0 TDI
engines.notes: Liquid but repair reserve required: belt, turbo, DPF/EGR, clutch/DMF.

engines.label: DSG/DQ200/S-tronic risk
engines.notes: Very strict. Needs clean shifting and proof.

generations.name: Golf 7
generations.notes: Strong buyer-service car, less cheap flip. It needs a real under-market price because buy-in is high. 5-door/Variant, TUV, service and clean history matter.

engines.label: 1.2/1.4 TSI EA211
engines.notes: Better than old EA111, but still verify service, turbo, oil use. DSG adds risk.

engines.label: 1.6 TDI
engines.notes: Good demand, but DPF/EGR/injectors and mileage matter.

engines.label: 2.0 TDI
engines.notes: Liquid but not cheap to fix. GTD/tuning needs extra caution.

engines.label: DSG/DQ200/DQ250 risk
engines.notes: Not automatic reject, but no strong lead without gearbox behavior/proof.

generations.name: Polo 9N
generations.notes: Old but very liquid only when cheap. TUV and rust/chain/cold-start decide. Above about 1700-2000 EUR it needs unusually clean condition.

engines.label: 1.2 3-cylinder petrol
engines.notes: Liquid but check chain/cold start, rough idle and oil leaks.

engines.label: 1.4 MPI petrol
engines.notes: Better cheap Polo engine profile. Good if TUV and body are clean.

engines.label: 1.4 TDI
engines.notes: Economical, but age, turbo, clutch and diesel system checks matter.

engines.label: automatic gearbox risk
engines.notes: Old automatic reduces resale safety; test hot/cold shifting.

generations.name: Polo 9N3
generations.notes: Still cheap and liquid. 5-door, TUV and Klima help a lot. Do not overpay just because it says VW.

engines.label: 1.2 petrol
engines.notes: Good only if chain/cold start is quiet and TUV is present.

engines.label: 1.4 petrol
engines.notes: Preferred older Polo petrol profile.

engines.label: 1.4/1.9 TDI
engines.notes: Economical and saleable, but turbo/clutch/diesel checks required.

engines.label: automatic gearbox risk
engines.notes: Old automatic must be tested carefully.

generations.name: Polo 6R
generations.notes: Very strong first-car/youth demand. Best: simple petrol, 5-door, TUV, Klima, stock condition. TSI/DSG must be strict.

engines.label: 1.2 MPI petrol
engines.notes: Best safe cheap 6R profile if not TSI/DSG.

engines.label: 1.4 MPI petrol
engines.notes: Good saleability, more pleasant than 1.2.

engines.label: 1.2 TSI EA111
engines.notes: Timing chain/turbo reputation. Need proof.

engines.label: 1.6 TDI
engines.notes: DPF/EGR/injector risk; okay only with proof and long TUV.

engines.label: DSG/DQ200 risk
engines.notes: Small-car DSG can destroy margin. No strong lead without proof.

generations.name: Polo 6C
generations.notes: Modern enough and very liquid for first-car buyers. Buy-in is higher, so it needs a real under-market price.

engines.label: 1.0 MPI petrol
engines.notes: Simple and youth-friendly if clean and serviced.

engines.label: 1.2/1.4 TSI EA211
engines.notes: Better than EA111 but still check service, oil, turbo; DSG adds risk.

engines.label: 1.4 TDI
engines.notes: Economical but DPF/EGR/turbo checks matter.

engines.label: DSG/DQ200 risk
engines.notes: No strong lead without gearbox proof and strong price.

generations.name: Corsa C
generations.notes: Very cheap beginner-car market. Only interesting with TUV, low entry price and simple petrol. Rust, chain noise and Easytronic can kill the deal.

engines.label: 1.0 petrol
engines.notes: Slow and less desirable. Needs cheap price, TUV and clean idle.

engines.label: 1.2 petrol
engines.notes: Saleable cheap Corsa engine. Check chain noise, oil leaks, misfire.

engines.label: 1.4 petrol
engines.notes: Best older Corsa petrol profile if body and TUV are good.

engines.label: 1.3 CDTI diesel
engines.notes: Only with proof and long TUV. Turbo/EGR/injector/clutch risk is too big for weak margin.

engines.label: Easytronic robot
engines.notes: Market fears it. Reject for strong leads unless extremely cheap with proof.

generations.name: Corsa D
generations.notes: Core cheap first-car flip. Best with 5 doors, TUV, Klima, simple 1.2/1.4 petrol. Do not overpay just because mileage is low.

engines.label: 1.0 petrol
engines.notes: Weak engine, lower desirability. Good only very cheap with TUV.

engines.label: 1.2 petrol
engines.notes: Good city first-car profile. Check chain on cold start, coil pack, oil leaks.

engines.label: 1.4 petrol
engines.notes: Preferred Corsa D profile. More desirable than 1.0/1.2 if price is not retail.

engines.label: 1.3 CDTI diesel
engines.notes: DPF/EGR/turbo/injector risk. Only with long TUV, proof and clear discount.

engines.label: 1.6 Turbo / OPC
engines.notes: Enthusiast car, insurance and abuse risk. Not a normal beginner flip.

engines.label: Easytronic robot
engines.notes: Hard to sell safely. No strong lead without proof and huge discount.

generations.name: Corsa E
generations.notes: Modern enough for young buyers and first-car service. Strong only if price is clearly under market. Simple petrol and good equipment matter.

engines.label: 1.2 petrol
engines.notes: Good simple Corsa E profile if TUV and service are present.

engines.label: 1.4 naturally aspirated petrol
engines.notes: Preferred safe Corsa E engine for resale if not turbo/OPC.

engines.label: 1.0 Turbo
engines.notes: Turbo/chain/service proof required. Not a blind strong lead.

engines.label: 1.4 Turbo
engines.notes: More fun but needs oil/turbo/cooling proof and clean test drive.

engines.label: 1.3 CDTI diesel
engines.notes: Emissions, DPF/EGR/turbo risk. Only with long TUV and strong price.

engines.label: Easytronic robot
engines.notes: Market resistance and repair risk. Avoid for normal leads.

global_flip_rules.pricing_logic: Corsa is liquid, but buyers are price-sensitive. A retail-priced Corsa is not a deal. Strong leads need TUV plus discount, or a cheap cosmetic problem with clear exit.

generations.name: Fiesta Mk5
generations.notes: Old cheap first-car market. Interesting only with TUV, cheap entry and simple petrol. Rust and weak maintenance matter more than mileage alone.

engines.label: 1.25 petrol
engines.notes: Very good simple Fiesta engine profile if TUV/body are good.

engines.label: 1.3 petrol
engines.notes: Simple but weaker/desirability lower. Needs cheap price.

engines.label: 1.4 petrol
engines.notes: Good if service/TUV are present.

engines.label: 1.4/1.6 TDCi diesel
engines.notes: Turbo/injector/EGR/clutch risk. Only with proof and discount.

engines.label: automatic gearbox risk
engines.notes: Old small Ford automatic reduces resale safety.

generations.name: Fiesta Mk6
generations.notes: Core Fiesta flip generation. 1.25 petrol with TUV is very saleable. EcoBoost and PowerShift need hard proof or should not be HOT.

engines.label: 1.25 petrol
engines.notes: Best Fiesta Mk6 cheap first-car profile. Strong if TUV, 5-door, Klima.

engines.label: 1.4 petrol
engines.notes: Good, simple and saleable.

engines.label: 1.6 petrol
engines.notes: More power and okay liquidity, but insurance/fuel slightly weaker.

engines.label: 1.0 EcoBoost
engines.notes: Wet belt/cooling risk. No strong lead without documented belt/service proof.

engines.label: 1.4/1.6 TDCi diesel
engines.notes: DPF/EGR/turbo/injector risk. Only if price and proof are strong.

engines.label: PowerShift automatic
engines.notes: Market fears it. Avoid for normal HOT leads.

generations.name: Fiesta Mk7
generations.notes: Modern and attractive, but often retail-priced. EcoBoost must have wet belt/service proof. Strong only with real discount.

engines.label: 1.1 petrol
engines.notes: Simpler than EcoBoost. Good beginner story if price is not retail.

engines.label: 1.0 EcoBoost
engines.notes: Wet belt proof required. Without proof it should not be a strong recommendation.

engines.label: 1.5 TDCi diesel
engines.notes: Diesel system risk; less beginner-market friendly.

engines.label: PowerShift automatic
engines.notes: Do not output as HOT without proof and discount.

global_flip_rules.pricing_logic: Fiesta sells fast only when it is a simple petrol with TUV and a real discount. A normal-price Fiesta is useful as a buyer-service lead, not as a flip HOT.

generations.name: Focus Mk1
generations.notes: Old cheap car. Only interesting very cheap with long TUV and clean rust situation. Not a premium lead unless entry price is very low.

engines.label: 1.6 petrol
engines.notes: Best old Focus profile. Check rust and timing belt history.

engines.label: 1.8/2.0 petrol
engines.notes: More power, okay if cheap. Fuel/insurance reduce beginner demand.

engines.label: 1.8 TDDi/TDCi diesel
engines.notes: Old diesel risk. Only with TUV and proof.

engines.label: automatic gearbox
engines.notes: Old automatic lowers resale safety.

generations.name: Focus Mk2
generations.notes: Strong cheap workhorse, especially Turnier/Kombi. Good for flip if 1.6 petrol, TUV, clean rust/body and price is clearly under market.

engines.label: 1.6 petrol
engines.notes: Best Mk2 Focus target. Good liquidity, cheap parts, simple enough.

engines.label: 1.8/2.0 petrol
engines.notes: Can be good, especially Kombi. Buyer pool smaller than 1.6.

engines.label: 1.6 TDCi
engines.notes: Turbo/injector/DPF/EGR risk. Needs proof and price.

engines.label: 1.8/2.0 TDCi
engines.notes: Useful workhorse but diesel repairs can kill cheap flip margin.

engines.label: automatic gearbox
engines.notes: Test shifts carefully. Manual is preferred.

generations.name: Focus Mk3
generations.notes: More modern and liquid, but many are retail priced. Best safe target is 1.6 Ti-VCT petrol manual. EcoBoost/PowerShift must be strict.

engines.label: 1.6 Ti-VCT petrol
engines.notes: Best Mk3 Focus first-car/family profile if manual and serviced.

engines.label: 1.0 EcoBoost
engines.notes: Wet belt/cooling risk. No HOT without proof of belt/service.

engines.label: 1.5/1.6 EcoBoost
engines.notes: Turbo/cooling abuse risk. Good only with proof and discount.

engines.label: 1.5/1.6 TDCi
engines.notes: DPF/EGR/turbo/injector risk. Okay only with proof, long TUV and strong price.

engines.label: 2.0 TDCi
engines.notes: Better for commuters but not youth first-car sweet spot.

engines.label: PowerShift automatic
engines.notes: Market fears it. Reject for normal HOT leads without strong proof.

generations.name: Focus Mk4
generations.notes: Modern but usually too expensive for cheap flip. Only interesting with large discount and clean simple exit. EcoBoost proof still matters.

engines.label: 1.0 EcoBoost
engines.notes: Needs documented service/wet belt logic. Not a blind strong lead.

engines.label: 1.5 EcoBoost
engines.notes: Better but still turbo/service risk.

engines.label: 1.5 EcoBlue diesel
engines.notes: Diesel emissions risk and weaker beginner buyer story.

engines.label: automatic
engines.notes: Needs proof/test drive. Manual easier to sell cheaply.

global_flip_rules.pricing_logic: Focus can be profitable when it is a useful Kombi/Turnier or simple petrol below market. Normal-priced Focus is common and should stay CHECK, not HOT.

generations.name: Fabia I
generations.notes: Old but useful cheap car. Combi is practical. Only interesting with TUV, simple petrol or proven 1.9 TDI, and low entry price.

engines.label: 1.2 HTP petrol
engines.notes: Common but chain/rough running risk. Needs TUV and cheap price.

engines.label: 1.4 MPI/16V petrol
engines.notes: Preferred old Fabia petrol profile.

engines.label: 1.9 SDI/TDI
engines.notes: Durable reputation, but age/turbo/clutch/rust proof needed.

engines.label: automatic gearbox
engines.notes: Old automatic lowers resale safety.

generations.name: Fabia II
generations.notes: Strong practical first-car/budget car, especially Combi. Best with 1.4/1.6 MPI petrol or proven diesel. TSI/DSG must be strict.

engines.label: 1.2 HTP petrol
engines.notes: Okay only if cheap, TUV and clean cold start.

engines.label: 1.4 MPI petrol
engines.notes: Best simple Fabia II petrol.

engines.label: 1.6 MPI petrol
engines.notes: Very good if price is right. More useful in Combi.

engines.label: 1.2 TSI EA111
engines.notes: Timing chain/turbo reputation. No HOT without proof.

engines.label: 1.4 TSI / RS
engines.notes: RS twincharged/DSG risk. Not normal flip material.

engines.label: 1.6 TDI
engines.notes: DPF/EGR/injector risk. Needs proof and discount.

engines.label: DSG/DQ200
engines.notes: Small VAG DSG risk. Reject for normal strong leads.

generations.name: Fabia III
generations.notes: Modern, very useful first-car/family small car. Strong with 1.0 MPI/1.2 TSI EA211, 5-door/Combi, TUV and real discount.

engines.label: 1.0 MPI petrol
engines.notes: Simple and desirable first-car profile.

engines.label: 1.2 TSI EA211
engines.notes: Better than old EA111, still needs service/turbo/oil proof.

engines.label: 1.4 TDI
engines.notes: Economical but diesel emissions/turbo risk.

engines.label: DSG/DQ200
engines.notes: No HOT without proof and clean test drive.

global_flip_rules.pricing_logic: Fabia is practical and liquid, but it is not exciting. It must be cheap, clean and easy to explain. Combi with long TUV is often better than a prettier hatch with weak proof.

generations.name: Atos / Atos Prime
generations.notes: Very cheap, simple city car. Interesting only with long TUV, clean rust situation and very low price. It is a fast cheap-transport lead, not a high-margin prestige car.

engines.label: 1.0/1.1 petrol
engines.notes: Simple cheap city-car engine. Check rust, clutch, oil leaks, cold start.

engines.label: automatic gearbox
engines.notes: Can sell to city buyers, but test shifting and keep margin conservative.

generations.name: i10 PA
generations.notes: Good cheap first-car car. Best with 5 doors, TUV 18+ months, Klima and 1.1/1.2 petrol. Low risk, but margin is usually moderate.

engines.label: 1.1 petrol
engines.notes: Very good cheap first-car profile.

engines.label: 1.2 petrol
engines.notes: Preferred PA engine if price is right.

engines.label: automatic gearbox
engines.notes: Not a hard reject, but test gearbox hot/cold.

generations.name: i10 IA
generations.notes: Very strong first-car product. Reliable image, cheap running costs, city demand. Strong only if price is below market, because many are dealer retail.

engines.label: 1.0 petrol
engines.notes: Good city first-car profile.

engines.label: 1.2 petrol
engines.notes: Best i10 IA profile: more pleasant and still cheap.

engines.label: automatic gearbox
engines.notes: Can be desirable for city buyers, but margin reserve needed.

global_flip_rules.pricing_logic: Hyundai i10/Atos is a low-risk fast-sale car. Profit comes from buying cheap and clean, not from huge market gaps. Long TUV and low running costs are the selling story.

generations.name: i20 PB
generations.notes: Strong first-car/youth alternative to Polo/Corsa/Fiesta. Best: 1.2 petrol, 5 doors, Klima, TUV, under 170k km. Very good if bought below market.

engines.label: 1.2 petrol
engines.notes: Best cheap i20 target. Simple, economical, good first-car story.

engines.label: 1.4 petrol
engines.notes: Good if price is right; slightly higher running cost.

engines.label: 1.4 CRDi diesel
engines.notes: Diesel emissions/turbo/injector risk. Needs proof and long TUV.

engines.label: automatic gearbox
engines.notes: Not automatic reject, but must test shifts and price carefully.

generations.name: i20 GB
generations.notes: Modern and very saleable. Good buyer-service car and potential flip if clearly under market. Best with 1.2 petrol manual, 5 doors, TUV and service.

engines.label: 1.2 petrol
engines.notes: Best safe i20 GB target.

engines.label: 1.4 petrol
engines.notes: Good and more comfortable, but price must be realistic.

engines.label: 1.0 T-GDI turbo
engines.notes: Not a hard reject, but needs service/turbo proof and clean test.

engines.label: 1.1/1.4 CRDi diesel
engines.notes: Diesel system risk and weaker first-car story.

engines.label: automatic/DCT
engines.notes: Needs clean test; manual is safer for cheap flip.

global_flip_rules.pricing_logic: Hyundai i20 is one of the better modern cheap first-car targets. Strong leads need realistic price, TUV and simple petrol. It can sell faster than older German cars because buyers fear fewer repairs.

generations.name: Yaris P9
generations.notes: One of the safest first-car stocks. 200k can be acceptable with service/TUV.

engines.label: 1.0/1.3 VVT-i
engines.notes: Reliable reputation; check clutch/rust/service.

generations.name: Yaris XP13
generations.notes: Strong safe buyer-service stock, but buy-in often high.

engines.label: 1.0/1.33 VVT-i
engines.notes: Good, but profit needs price discipline.

generations.name: Aygo 1 / C1 / 107
generations.notes: Safe small first-car stock. Long TUV makes it easy to sell.

engines.label: 1.0 petrol
engines.notes: Reliable/simple; check clutch/exhaust/rust/TUV.

generations.name: A3 8P
generations.notes: Looks premium and liquid, but TFSI/DSG/S-tronic can kill margin. TUV required.

engines.label: 1.6 MPI
engines.notes: Safer A3 profile if manual and clean.

engines.label: TFSI / S-tronic / DSG
engines.notes: High market fear; no HOT without proof.

generations.name: A3 8V
generations.notes: Buyer-service stock, not cheap flip. Needs deep discount and clean tech.

engines.label: TSI/TDI
engines.notes: Good market but expensive repairs; proof needed.
